title: Anchored Curves, Tiled Heights, WordArt, Held Buttons & CSS-Chosen Icons
description: Five demos that hand the arithmetic to CSS: anchored connectors, tile-rounded heights, SVG WordArt, five microinteractions and icons as tokens.

drops.title: The Curve Between Them
drops.description: Three pairs of draggable dots joined by a curve that no element actually draws.
drops.concept: Each pair owns four absolutely positioned boxes whose insets are anchored between the two dots, so only the one matching the current diagonal has a non-zero size; the other three collapse and a style query removes them outright. border-shape paints an S-curve across the survivor using shape() with a smooth mirror, and because the close-range variant keeps the same command list, the flattening transitions instead of snapping.
drops.source: blog.master.dev — Two Circles, One Connection, and border-shape

interaction.mouse: Drag any of the six dots; the connector re-draws live and flips quadrant as the diagonal changes.
interaction.click: Sliders set stroke width, bow of the control point, and dot size.
interaction.touch: Pointer capture means dragging works the same on a touchscreen.

drops.title: A Height That Ends on a Tile
drops.description: A section that rounds its own auto height up to a whole number of background tiles.
drops.concept: A repeating background has a grain and a box's auto height does not, so the last row of the pattern gets sliced. calc-size(auto, round(up, size, var(--tile-h))) resolves the element's own auto height and snaps it to the tile step, with the block padding rounded to the same step. Flip between auto, round down and round up and the ratio under each panel goes from fractional to whole.
drops.source: Ahmad Shadeed — Fit height to background pattern size with calc-size()

interaction.mouse: Drag the word count and watch three panels hold their height, then take a whole tile at once.
interaction.click: Switch between auto, round down and round up to see the same content land on three heights.
interaction.touch: Panels reflow to one column; the snapping is unchanged.

drops.title: Make Text Like It's 1997
drops.description: WordArt rebuilt from a textPath, a stamped extrusion, a gradient and four filter primitives.
drops.concept: Every part of the 1997 title treatment has a plain vector equivalent: the arch and the wave are a <textPath> riding a quadratic whose control point is a slider, the 3-D is the same string stamped back along the light angle and darkened, the chrome is a vertical <linearGradient>, and the bevel is feOffset plus feFlood plus feComposite merged under the glyph. Six styles, three on screen at once, all driven by one text field.
drops.source: TitleArt by Davey Barker — make text like it's 1997

interaction.mouse: Type in the field and all three slabs re-render; pick a style chip and the stack rotates through the gallery.
interaction.click: Sliders control warp, extrusion depth, light angle and size; a checkbox toggles the gradient sweep.
interaction.touch: The panel hides on small screens and the gallery chips remain tappable.

drops.title: Five Ways to Answer a Click
drops.description: Hold-to-delete, drag-to-scrub, staggered letters, a pointer-tracked border and a checkbox with overshoot.
drops.concept: Five microinteractions reduced to the mechanism each one actually needs: a width transition whose duration is the commit threshold, a captured pointer turning horizontal travel into a value, per-letter transition-delay driven by a --i index, two custom properties feeding a radial gradient behind a 1.4px rim, and a cubic-bezier that overshoots 1. Each card shows three instances, because one instance is a demo and three is a pattern.

interaction.mouse: Press and hold a file row to delete it, drag a field label sideways to scrub it, hover the buttons for the letter swap and the edge glow.
interaction.click: A panel retimes everything at once: speed, stagger, hold duration and glow radius.
interaction.touch: Every interaction is pointer-based, so hold and scrub both work with a finger.

drops.title: Icons the Stylesheet Chooses
drops.description: Icons as design tokens: a masked pseudo-element, a style query guard and inherits: false.
drops.concept: Each icon is a custom property holding an inline SVG, a component points its --icon at one, and an empty pseudo-element filled with currentColor is masked into that shape. A @container style(--icon-start) query keeps the rule from firing on elements that never asked for an icon, and registering the property with inherits: false is what stops a nested <strong> from sprouting one of its own — the demo shows the unguarded version next to it, growing three icons where you asked for one.
drops.source: Lea Verou — The best way to use icons in web UIs

interaction.mouse: Hover Delete and the component swaps its token on :hover; the colour pills show the mask taking currentColor.
interaction.click: A select changes the default --icon for every component at once, with no markup change.
interaction.touch: Cards stack to one column; the comparison panel stays side by side above 620px.
